stem: What is a distinguishing feature of the onset of otitis media in Aboriginal children compared with non-Aboriginal children?

options.text: It can be seen as early as one week of age in Aboriginal children
It typically begins only after preschool or daycare starts
It is less common but usually more severe in Aboriginal children
It is usually caused by different bacterial pathogens
It usually does not occur until after 6 months of age

explanation: Early-onset otitis media is characteristic in Aboriginal children. This is because it may be seen as early as one week of age, much earlier than in many non-Aboriginal children.

optionExplanations.A: Correct because otitis media may be present from as early as one week of age in Aboriginal children.
optionExplanations.B: Incorrect because onset can occur in early infancy, well before preschool or daycare age.
optionExplanations.C: Incorrect because Aboriginal children have a higher burden of otitis media, not a lower prevalence.
optionExplanations.D: Incorrect because the key distinguishing feature is the very early onset, not a different primary pathogen pattern.
optionExplanations.E: Incorrect because otitis media can occur much earlier than 6 months of age in Aboriginal children.

source.hint: Think about how early in life the infection first appears in remote communities.
